symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of vertices in the fixed experimental network.

symbols.name: \mathbb A
symbols.def: The two exposure labels \(\mathbb A=\{1,0\}\).

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: A generic label, with \(a=1\) denoting the focal exposure and \(a=0\) denoting the comparison exposure.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The fixed adjacency matrix on the \(n\) experimental units.

symbols.name: \nu
symbols.def: The randomization distribution chosen before outcomes are observed.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: The treatment vector drawn from \(\nu\).

symbols.name: f_i
symbols.def: The exposure mapping induced by \(G\) for unit \(i\).

symbols.name: Y_i(w)
symbols.def: The potential outcome of unit \(i\) under assignment \(w\).

symbols.name: D_{i,a}
symbols.def: The indicator \(D_{i,a}=\mathbf 1\{f_i(W)=a\}\).

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: The vector \(D=(D_{1,1},\ldots,D_{n,1},D_{1,0},\ldots,D_{n,0})^{\top}\).

symbols.name: \pi_{i,a}
symbols.def: The known probability \(\pi_{i,a}=\mathbb E_{\nu}[D_{i,a}]\).

symbols.name: \Pi
symbols.def: The diagonal matrix whose diagonal is \((\pi_{1,1},\ldots,\pi_{n,1},\pi_{1,0},\ldots,\pi_{n,0})\).

symbols.name: \Omega
symbols.def: The known matrix \(\Omega=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu}(D)\).

symbols.name: Y_i(a)
symbols.def: The potential outcome of unit \(i\) under exposure label \(a\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The superpopulation law of the pair \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) used only for ex ante basis choice.

symbols.name: F_a
symbols.def: The marginal law of \(Y_i(a)\) under \(H\).

symbols.name: F_1
symbols.def: The marginal \(F_a\) at \(a=1\).

symbols.name: F_0
symbols.def: The marginal \(F_a\) at \(a=0\).

symbols.name: \Gamma(F_1,F_0)
symbols.def: The class \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)=\{H\in\mathcal P([0,1]^2):\operatorname{marg}(H)=(F_1,F_0)\}\).

symbols.name: F_a^{-1}
symbols.def: The generalized inverse of the marginal distribution function.

symbols.name: \mu_a
symbols.def: The mean \(\mu_a=\int y\,dF_a(y)\).

symbols.name: \sigma_a^2
symbols.def: The variance \(\sigma_a^2=\int(y-\mu_a)^2\,dF_a(y)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C(F_1,F_0)
symbols.def: The covariance image \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=\{\operatorname{Cov}_H(Y_i(1),Y_i(0)):H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\}\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: The scalar \(c=\operatorname{Cov}_H(Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) for \(H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\).

symbols.name: Q(c)
symbols.def: For \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the matrix \(Q(c)=\begin{bmatrix}\mu_1^2\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}+\sigma_1^2I_n&-\mu_1\mu_0\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}-cI_n\\-\mu_1\mu_0\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}-cI_n&\mu_0^2\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}+\sigma_0^2I_n\end{bmatrix}\).

symbols.name: b_1
symbols.def: The coefficients multiplying the focal-exposure indicators.

symbols.name: b_0
symbols.def: The coefficients multiplying the comparison-exposure indicators.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The matrix \(B(b_1,b_0)=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).

symbols.name: S_B
symbols.def: The matrix \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\).

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: A fixed lower bound on the normalized smallest eigenvalue of \(S_B\).

symbols.name: \widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z
symbols.type: maximal well-defined ordinary-inverse Zhao-type matrix domain
symbols.def: The unquotiented block-separable matrices \(B\) satisfying \(B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\), which is the maximal domain on which the ordinary inverse in Zhao's Equation (8) is defined.

symbols.name: \mathcal B_Z
symbols.def: The quotient of \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) by independent nonzero arm-column rescaling; equivalently, the scale-quotiented block-separable bases for which \(S_B\) is positive definite.

symbols.name: \mathcal B_\kappa
symbols.def: The compact normalized subclass with \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)\ge\kappa\).

symbols.name: g_B(c)
symbols.def: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the Zhao gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right]\).

symbols.name: \ell_B(c)
symbols.def: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), the residual \(\ell_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]-g_B(c)\).

symbols.name: r(B)
symbols.def: The diagnostic \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\).

symbols.name: w(B)
symbols.def: The primary loss \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\).

symbols.name: v^\star
symbols.def: The diagnostic value \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_R
symbols.def: The diagnostic correspondence \(\mathcal A_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_0
symbols.def: The correspondence \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)\) on the fixed normalized regular projective class; it is not Zhao's optimizer correspondence on the published unquotiented domain.
symbols.role: zero-covariance optimizer on the fixed \(\kappa\)-regular class

symbols.name: m_a
symbols.def: The number of independent unpaired pilot outcomes observed under exposure label \(a\).

symbols.name: Y^{P}_{j,a}
symbols.def: The \(j\)-th independent pilot draw from \(F_a\), with no cross-arm pairing.

symbols.name: \widehat F_a
symbols.def: The empirical law \(\widehat F_a=m_a^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m_a}\delta_{Y^P_{j,a}}\).

symbols.name: \widehat r(B)
symbols.def: The diagnostic obtained by substituting empirical marginal moments and endpoints into \(r(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat v
symbols.def: The diagnostic value \(\widehat v=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathcal A}_R
symbols.def: The diagnostic set \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\).

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: The requested numerical optimality gap.

symbols.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}
symbols.def: An exact rational or real-algebraic encoding, or certified inclusion-oracle encoding with effective refinement moduli and exact feasibility decisions, of the known design matrices, both endpoint moment matrices, endpoint covariances, regularity threshold, and tolerance.

symbols.name: h_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: The maximum projective-chart diameter of a box retained at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

symbols.name: \xi
symbols.def: The instance \(\xi=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) with \(G\) and the exposure maps held fixed.

symbols.name: \mathfrak X_\kappa
symbols.def: The relatively topologized class of instances satisfying the named predicates ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility.

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: The causal contrast \(\tau=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)\}\).

symbols.name: h(c)
symbols.def: For \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\).

symbols.name: v_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).

symbols.name: B_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: An exactly feasible basis used to certify an upper bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\).

symbols.name: L_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A rational lower bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) obtained from outward-rounded lower bounds over all retained feasible boxes.

symbols.name: U_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A rational upper bound on \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) certified by an exactly feasible incumbent and outward rounding.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The correspondence \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_\varepsilon
symbols.def: The union of unpruned quotient-chart boxes, required to contain \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\).

symbols.name: \mathscr K_{\varepsilon}
symbols.def: A checkable record of the chart cover, feasible incumbent, minimization bounds, retained outer boxes, exact infeasibility or lower-bound pruning records, and mesh.

symbols.name: \Delta(\xi)
symbols.def: The gap \(\Delta(\xi)=\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_\xi(B_0)-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_\xi(B_{\mathrm{mm}})\).

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: A positive certified lower bound on \(\Delta(\xi)\).

symbols.name: \eta
symbols.def: A uniform positive lower bound on normalized nondegeneracy above \(\kappa\) over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\cup\mathcal A_0\).

symbols.name: \widehat w(B)
symbols.def: The endpoint residual criterion obtained by substituting the empirical marginal moments and Frechet covariance endpoints into \(w(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The value \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}
symbols.def: The set \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B_Z^+
symbols.type: novel Moore--Penrose completion of the Zhao-type projective basis class
symbols.def: The note's novel rank-stratified completion of \(\mathcal B_Z\) that permits zero arm columns and uses Moore--Penrose inversion; it is not Zhao's domain.

symbols.name: S_B^+
symbols.def: The Moore--Penrose inverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\).

symbols.name: g_B^+(c)
symbols.def: The Zhao-form gain extended by the Moore--Penrose inverse \(S_B^+\) on the novel completion.

symbols.name: \ell_B^+(c)
symbols.def: The residual \(h(c)-g_B^+(c)\) on the novel completion.

symbols.name: w^+(B)
symbols.def: The maximum of \(\ell_B^+(c_L)\) and \(\ell_B^+(c_U)\).

symbols.name: v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
symbols.def: The minimum of \(w^+(B)\) over \(\mathcal B_Z^+\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
symbols.def: The argmin of \(w^+(B)\) over the novel completion.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_0^+
symbols.def: The argmax of \(g_B^+(0)\) over the novel completion.

symbols.name: \iota
symbols.def: The map sending an ordinary projective class to the same representative in the novel Moore--Penrose completion.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)
symbols.def: The set \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\) with the threshold shown explicitly.

symbols.name: Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}
symbols.def: The realized outcome \(Y_i(W)\) in the main experiment.

symbols.name: \widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
symbols.def: The vector with entries \(D_{i,1}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}/\pi_{i,1}\) in the first block and \(-D_{i,0}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}/\pi_{i,0}\) in the second block.

symbols.name: \widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
symbols.def: The coefficient \(S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\).

symbols.name: \widehat 1_a
symbols.def: The average \(n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,a}/\pi_{i,a}\), when its denominator is positive.

symbols.name: \widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)
symbols.def: The armwise self-normalized version of \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)\) defined in the observable map.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
symbols.def: The Horvitz--Thompson exposure-effect estimator minus the chosen coefficient times the centered basis exposure statistic.

symbols.name: \mathcal J_{\mathrm{PICC}}
symbols.type: reproducible unexecuted Jiangxi PICC reanalysis protocol
symbols.def: The data-ingestion, network reconstruction, exposure enumeration, robust optimization, ordinary-inverse estimator, and audit-output protocol for the Cai--de Janvry--Sadoulet experiment; no numerical table is asserted.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: The vector \(Y=(Y_1(1),\ldots,Y_n(1),-Y_1(0),\ldots,-Y_n(0))^{\top}\).

symbols.name: q_Z
symbols.def: The map \(q_Z(B)=[B]\) that quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two arm columns.

assumptions.condition: For every unit \(i\) and assignments \(w,w'\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(f_i(w)=f_i(w')\) implies \(Y_i(w)=Y_i(w')\).
For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
The \(n\) pairs \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) have joint law \(H^{\otimes n}\).

standard.name: Independent and identically distributed potential-outcome pairs, Zhao Assumption 3\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 22

assumptions.condition: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
The ordered pair of marginals of \(H\) equals \((F_1,F_0)\).
The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).

standard.name: Sharp Fréchet covariance range, Aronow--Green--Lee Lemma 1

assumptions.condition: The pair \(\left(F_1\otimes F_0,\operatorname{Cov}_{F_1\otimes F_0}\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)\) belongs to \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\times\{0\}\).

standard.name: Independent product coupling with zero covariance
Supplied-basis control-variate nondegeneracy, Zhao Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21

assumptions.condition: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).

novel.justification: Independent rescaling of either basis column leaves Zhao's control-variate span and gain unchanged, so this condition selects compact representatives without restricting implementable estimators.

standard.name: Supplied-basis nondegeneracy, fixed-threshold variant of Zhao Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) on p. 21

assumptions.condition: There exist vectors \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\) and \(\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B\}\ge\kappa\) for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).

novel.justification: This is a verifiable design-side condition: for a fixed network, exposure maps, and known randomization, the matrix \(\Omega\) is known before outcomes are observed, so nonemptiness of the normalized \(\kappa\)-regular projective class can be certified as part of design preparation. Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\) regulates a supplied basis and does not assert existence of such a normalized feasible basis.

assumptions.condition: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).

novel.justification: Separate exposure-specific historical samples are available in insurance and public-health deployments even when privacy or record linkage prevents cross-arm pairing; independence from the later randomized assignment is ensured by collecting or freezing those archives before randomization. Mikhaeil and Green inform consistency of empirical marginal endpoints, not this product sampling law.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_Z
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_\kappa
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.

definitions.name: h(c),g_B(c),\ell_B(c)
definitions.construction: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).

definitions.name: r(B),w(B),v^\star,v_{\mathrm{mm}}
definitions.construction: Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary maximin-gain diagnostics.  The primary robust loss and minimax value are \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).

definitions.name: \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}},\mathcal A_R,\mathcal A_0
definitions.construction: On the feasible covariance domain, where ass:product-coupling-zero and ass:frechet-covariance-domain give \(0\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\), retain \(\mathcal A_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) as the secondary maximin-gain correspondence, define the primary minimax-residual correspondence \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\), and define the ordinarily typed zero-covariance surrogate correspondence \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}
definitions.construction: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.

definitions.name: \mathscr K_{\varepsilon}
definitions.construction: A corrected minimax certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) consists of a finite quotient-chart cover, an exactly feasible incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\), rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}\), outward-rounded endpoint-loss and constraint bounds for every retained box, a checkable exact-infeasibility or valid lower-bound pruning record for every discarded box, retained boxes whose union is \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), and their maximum chart diameter \(h_{\varepsilon}\).  The exactly feasible incumbent may be represented by exact rational or real-algebraic coordinates, or by a certified inclusion-oracle name whose every requested precision terminates.  For the latter representation, exact feasibility is certified by nested closed quotient-chart boxes, each meeting \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), whose diameters tend to zero and whose intersection is the singleton \(\{B_{\varepsilon}\}\).  The checker requires \(L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon}\), \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_\varepsilon\); it never accepts deletion of a box meeting the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary without an exact infeasibility certificate or a valid objective lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound.

definitions.name: projective interval branch-and-bound procedure
definitions.construction: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators.  For any chart box whose feasible intersection is nonempty, repeated bisection and exact feasible-child selection produce nested closed feasible boxes with diameters tending to zero; their singleton intersection supplies the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible incumbent authorized by the certificate definition.  The procedure prunes only by exact infeasibility or by a certified box lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound, and it refines the finite quotient-chart cover and arithmetic enclosures until \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), at which point it returns the full certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\).

definitions.name: \widehat w,\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}},\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}
definitions.construction: Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\); substitute them into \(Q(c_L),Q(c_U)\), \(h(c)\), \(g_B(c)\), and \(\ell_B(c)\).  Retain the resulting \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\) only as secondary diagnostics.  Define \(\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\}\), \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak X_\kappa
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak X_\kappa=\{\xi=(\nu,F_1,F_0):\operatorname{ass{:}exposure\mbox{-}positivity}(\xi)\wedge\operatorname{ass{:}kappa\mbox{-}feasibility}(\xi)\wedge F_1,F_0\in\mathcal P([0,1])\}\) is carved by the single named positivity and feasibility predicates, with the relative topology inherited from total variation on the finite assignment simplex and the Wasserstein metric on each bounded marginal.

definitions.name: \Delta(\xi)
definitions.construction: \(\Delta(\xi)=\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_{\xi}(B_0)-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_{\xi}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})\).  Since every member of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\) has loss \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\), the second term equals \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\).

definitions.name: finite lawful minimax separation handle
definitions.construction: Start from a three-vertex network under independent Bernoulli assignment with probability \(1/3\), enumerate the mutually exclusive exposure truth tables exactly, derive exact \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), use Bernoulli \(1/2\) pilot marginals, and analyze simultaneously the full minimax-residual and zero-covariance-surrogate correspondences.  The instance-specific certificate consists of exact optimizer equality sets, a rational lower bound \(\delta>0\) on \(\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}\), and a rational optimizer-wide regularity slack \(\eta>0\) over \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\cup\mathcal A_0\).  This finite lawful separation handle is distinct from, and does not assert, generic finite-\(\varepsilon\) termination of the moment-complete projective interval branch-and-bound procedure.

definitions.name: \widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z,q_Z
definitions.construction: \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z=\{B:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,\ B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\}\).  This is the maximal block-separable matrix domain on which the ordinary inverse in Zhao's Equation (8) is well defined; it is implicit in that formula and is not claimed to be a separately named domain in Zhao.  Define the quotient map \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) by \(q_Z(B)=[B]\).

definitions.name: \widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}},\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{SN}},\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
definitions.construction:
For observed outcomes \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(f_i(W))\), define Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson outcome stack
\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]
For a supplied basis \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\), Zhao's Section 3.3 ordinary-inverse coefficient map is
\[
\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
Thus the signed observed stack is already inverse-probability weighted and the formula applies the additional \(\Pi^{-1}\); in particular
\(\mathbb E_\nu[B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}]
=B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y\).
For \(a\in\{1,0\}\), set \(\widehat1_a=n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,a}/\pi_{i,a}\), and define \(\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)=\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)/\widehat1_a\) when \(\widehat1_a>0\), and zero otherwise.  The deployed minimax basis belongs to \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), hence has an ordinary-invertible representative.  Deploy
\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.
\]

definitions.name: \mathcal J_{\mathrm{PICC}}
definitions.construction: The exploratory record \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{PICC}}\) is the reproducible but unexecuted procedure implemented by \(\texttt{discovery/jiangxi\_robust\_reanalysis.py}\).  Its input directory must contain the Dataverse-converted tables \(\texttt{survey.tab}\) and \(\texttt{network.tab}\), which are the filenames the script actually consumes.  The procedure cleans identifiers, sentinel \(99\), self-loops, and duplicate directed nominations while retaining cross-village nominations, constructs the three target populations for \(\tau_{10},\tau_{21},\tau_{32}\), and uses the disclosed independent Bernoulli \((1/2)\) reconstruction necessitated by the unreleased original strata.  It splits connected components of the exposure-overlap graph without cutting components, estimates the two marginal laws and Fr\'echet endpoints on each training fold, and optimizes robust and zero-covariance bases under the same initialization list and iteration budget.  Each held-out basis is deployed through def:observable-coefficient-map with Zhao's ordinary inverse and the additional \(\Pi^{-1}\) factor; no Moore--Penrose safeguard is used or attributed to Zhao.  The output fields report point estimates, design-randomization standard errors, both endpoint losses, worst loss, minimum regularity, and a heuristic objective diagnostic.  The latter is not a certified upper-minus-lower optimization gap.  The authenticated replication data were unavailable in the solve environment, so the protocol was not executed and no numerical table is asserted.  It remains exploratory because its internal cross-fitting is not the independent unpaired pilot of ass:unpaired-pilot.

definitions.name: \mathcal B_Z^+
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B_Z^+=\{[B]_+:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where two representatives are equivalent when, separately for each arm, both columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  This is the note's novel rank-zero/rank-one/rank-two Moore--Penrose completion of \(\mathcal B_Z\); it is not Zhao's domain and attributes no singular carrier or pseudoinverse construction to Zhao.

definitions.name: g_B^+(c),\ell_B^+(c),w^+(B),v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
definitions.construction:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) be the Moore--Penrose inverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\operatorname*{argmin}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
These are objects of the note's novel completion, not formulas or a domain attributed to Zhao.

statements.statement: Under ass:known-exposure, ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, and ass:iid-potential-pairs, every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) has affine functions \(c\mapsto g_B(c)\) and \(c\mapsto\ell_B(c)\) on the imported feasible domain \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\). Consequently, \(\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}\ell_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\), with both extrema attained. The product coupling gives \(c_L\le0\le c_U\), so \(g_B(0)\) is an ordinarily typed feasible-covariance gain. If \(c_L<0<c_U\), \(g_B(0)=\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})\) if and only if the affine slope of \(g_B\) is zero.
statements.justification: The theorem imports the published Fréchet range and proves its exact affine reduction inside Zhao's basis objective.
statements.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, Lemma 1, already gives the sharp covariance range. Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Theorem 4 and equation (8) on pp. 22--23, gives the covariance-dependent basis objective, and the paragraph following Theorem 4 on p. 23 substitutes the feasible zero-covariance surrogate matrix; neither source derives the affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside this projective objective.
statements.consumer: An experimenter with only two pilot marginals can evaluate the exact worst-copula gain of any proposed network basis.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), def:zhao-basis-class gives \(S_B\succ0\), so \(S_B^{-1}\) exists.  Put
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\ I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
By def:moment-matrix, \(Q(c)=Q(0)-cE\).  Cyclicity and linearity of trace therefore give
\[
g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\{A_BQ(0)\}
-cn^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_BE),                                      \tag{1}
\]
which is affine in \(c\).

We also compute the uncontrolled term without importing another statement.  Write
\(M=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\) in its two exposure blocks.  Mutual exclusivity gives
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu}(D_{i,1},D_{i,0})
=\mathbb E_{\nu}(D_{i,1}D_{i,0})-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}
=-\pi_{i,1}\pi_{i,0}.
\]
Consequently, the \(i\)-th diagonal entries of both off-diagonal blocks of \(M\) equal \(-1\).  Hence
\[
\operatorname{tr}(ME)=-2n
\]
and
\[
h(c)-h(0)
=-cn^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(ME)
=\frac{2c}{n}.                                                        \tag{2}
\]
Equations (1)--(2) and \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\) show that \(\ell_B\) is affine as well.  Ass:known-exposure and ass:iid-potential-pairs supply the causal exposure and ex ante moment interpretations; the affine conclusion itself follows from the displayed matrix identities.

By ass:frechet-covariance-domain,
\[
\left\{\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}:H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\right\}
=[c_L,c_U].                                                          \tag{3}
\]
An affine function on a compact interval attains its minimum and maximum at an endpoint.  Because (3) is equality of sets, each endpoint is the covariance of at least one coupling in \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\).  Applying this observation to \(g_B\) and \(\ell_B\) proves the two endpoint formulas and attainment.  Ass:product-coupling-zero supplies a coupling in \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\) with covariance zero; (3) then yields \(c_L\le0\le c_U\), so \(g_B(0)\) is evaluated at a feasible covariance.

Finally write \(g_B(c)=\alpha_B+\beta_Bc\).  If \(\beta_B=0\), the gain is constant, so its value at zero is its infimum.  Conversely, suppose \(c_L<0<c_U\).  If \(\beta_B>0\), then \(g_B(c_L)<g_B(0)\); if \(\beta_B<0\), then \(g_B(c_U)<g_B(0)\).  Thus \(g_B(0)\) is the worst-coupling gain if and only if the affine slope \(\beta_B\) is zero. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For every \(\kappa>0\), the quotient \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is compact and satisfies \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).  Conversely, every \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\) has normalized representatives belonging to \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) for some basis-dependent \(\kappa>0\), so
\[
\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa=\mathcal B_Z,
\qquad
q_Z^{-1}\!\left(\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa\right)=\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z.
\]
Thus the threshold classes exhaust the maximal well-defined ordinary-inverse block-separable domain implicit in Zhao's Equation (8), modulo the exact independent nonzero column-rescaling fibers of \(q_Z\).  Each fixed \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is a threshold-restricted subclass, although strict inclusion is not universal, and no singular or Moore--Penrose basis is covered.
statements.justification: The proposition states exactly how compact threshold classes exhaust the maximal ordinary-inverse Zhao-type matrix domain modulo rescaling.
statements.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates regulates a supplied basis but does not construct the compact projective threshold exhaustion or prove its exact transfer back to all ordinary-invertible matrix representatives.
statements.consumer: A global solver can report its threshold while retaining a certified statement about the full ordinary-inverse matrix domain modulo rescaling.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
K_\kappa=\left\{(b_1,b_0):\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n,
\ \lambda_{\min}\!\left(n^{-1}B(b_1,b_0)^{\top}\Omega B(b_1,b_0)\right)\ge\kappa\right\}.
\]
The product of the two radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres is compact.  The displayed matrix and its smallest eigenvalue depend continuously on \((b_1,b_0)\), so \(K_\kappa\) is closed and compact.  After normalization, independent sign changes are the residual projective identifications.  The quotient map is continuous; hence its image \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is compact.

If \([B]\in\mathcal B_\kappa\), then
\[
\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge n\kappa>0.
\]
Thus \(S_B\) is positive definite, and def:zhao-basis-class gives \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\).

Conversely, take \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\).  Positive definiteness forces both basis columns to be nonzero.  Put
\[
d_a=\frac{\sqrt n}{\lVert b_a\rVert_2},\qquad
T=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_0),\qquad
\widetilde B=BT.
\]
Then \(\widetilde B\) is a normalized representative of the same projective class and
\[
S_{\widetilde B}=T^{\top}S_BT\succ0.
\]
Consequently \(\rho_B=\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_{\widetilde B})>0\).  Taking \(\kappa_B=\rho_B/2\) gives \([B]\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_B}\), and therefore
\[
\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa=\mathcal B_Z. \tag{1}
\]
By thm:zhao-ordinary-domain-quotient-transfer, \(q_Z\) is onto \(\mathcal B_Z\) and its domain is exactly \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\).  Taking the inverse image of (1) proves the second displayed equality.  The proof uses only positive-definite ordinary inverses.  The qualifier about strictness is necessary: the definitions imply inclusion, but in a design with a uniform positive normalized eigenvalue bound a sufficiently small threshold can leave the quotient unchanged. \(\square\)

statements.statement: If \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) satisfies \(\Delta(\xi_0)>0\) and there is \(\eta>0\) such that \(\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\}\ge\eta\), then there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) of \(\xi_0\) such that \(\Delta(\xi)>0\) for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\).
statements.justification: Persistence upgrades any exact finite witness from a curiosity to a nondegenerate region of lawful experiments.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals gives continuity of fixed-marginal coupling correspondences, while GaoKleywegt2017DependenceRobust gives a general dependence-robust decision template; neither proves strict robust-basis dominance for Zhao's optimizer correspondences.
statements.consumer: Any certified output of oeq:separated-lawful-witness with \(\delta>0\) and optimizer-wide slack \(\eta>0\) activates this theorem and yields a relative-open region on which every robust optimizer has lower worst-copula residual variance than every zero-covariance-surrogate optimizer.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(\delta_0=\Delta(\xi_0)>0\).  The displayed optimizer-wide eigenvalue slack is exactly the hypothesis of lem:dominance-gap-lower-semicontinuity.  If no relative-open neighborhood of \(\xi_0\) had positive gap, then, because the relative total-variation--Wasserstein topology in def:lawful-instance-class is metrizable, for each positive integer \(j\) one could choose \(\xi_j\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) within distance \(1/j\) of \(\xi_0\) and satisfying \(\Delta(\xi_j)\le0\).  Thus \(\xi_j\to\xi_0\), and the lemma would imply
\[
0<\delta_0=\Delta(\xi_0)
\le\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)
\le0,
\]
a contradiction.  Hence some relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) of \(\xi_0\) satisfies \(\Delta(\xi)>0\) throughout. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Fix \(G,\nu,(f_i)_{i=1}^n\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility, so \(\mathcal B_\kappa\neq\varnothing\).  Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, as \(m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty\), \(\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\to0\) almost surely, \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}\to v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely, and every subsequential limit of \(B_m\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely.  Equivalently, \(\limsup_{m_1,m_0\to\infty}\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely in the projective quotient.
statements.justification: The set-valued conclusion is the strongest valid generic guarantee when projective symmetries or endpoint ties create multiple optimizers.
statements.gap: AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance and MikhaeilGreen2024SharpRegressionAdjustment prove scalar endpoint consistency; Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates, Theorem 3, concerns estimated-coefficient consistency and asymptotics but does not establish uniform global basis-objective or argmax-correspondence consistency.
statements.consumer: An independent historical or external pilot can select a robust network basis without pretending that its two marginal samples identify a cross-world copula.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\{B^\star\}\) in the projective quotient, then every measurable selection \(\widehat B\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) converges almost surely to \(B^\star\).  Without the singleton condition, there exist bounded two-marginal instances satisfying the maintained assumptions for which the outer-set conclusion of thm:plugin-correspondence holds but some measurable plug-in selections fail to converge to a point.
statements.justification: This proposition draws the exact line between defensible set consistency and unjustified point consistency.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals implies upper hemicontinuity for optimizer sets but does not give this pilot-based quotient-space selection result or its tie counterexample.
statements.consumer: Applied reporting can retain all empirically indistinguishable robust bases unless an isolated unique saddle is actually verified.

statements.statement:
There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness.  Let \(n=3\), let
\[
G=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&1\\1&1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\nu(w)=\left(\frac13\right)^{\sum_iw_i}
       \left(\frac23\right)^{3-\sum_iw_i},
\]
and, writing \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact design and endpoint inputs are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For normalized representatives \(B(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}x&0\\0&y\end{bmatrix}\), the full optimizer correspondences are
\[
\mathcal A_0=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=\mathbf 1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0
\right\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,\ 
(\mathbf 1^{\top}y)^2=\frac{216}{55}
\right\}.
\]
They are nonempty, and their exact objective values satisfy
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad
w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200}\quad(B_0\in\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432}
\quad(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}).
\]
Moreover every member of \(\mathcal A_0\cup\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) obeys
\[
\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}.
\]
Consequently \(\xi_0=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and the rational choices
\[
\delta=\frac{4912}{39525},
\qquad
\eta=\frac5{216}
\]
give the full-correspondence certificates
\[
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_0)
-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=\delta>0
\]
and
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}
=\eta>0.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Write \(\mathbf1=\mathbf1_3\).  Enumeration of the eight assignments gives the following exposure events.  The all-zero and all-one assignments expose no unit to either displayed label.  If only unit \(i\) is treated, then \(D_{i,1}=1\) and \(D_{j,0}=1\) for the other two units.  If exactly \(i,j\) are treated, then \(D_{k,0}=1\).  Hence
\[
\pi_{i,1}=\frac4{27},
\qquad
\pi_{i,0}=2\frac4{27}+\frac2{27}=\frac{10}{27}.
\]
Direct intersection probabilities give, for \(i\ne j\),
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
&i=j&i\ne j\\ \hline
\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu}(D_{i,1},D_{j,1})&92/729&-16/729\\
\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu}(D_{i,1},D_{j,0})&-40/729&68/729\\
\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu}(D_{i,0},D_{j,0})&170/729&8/729.
\end{array}
\]
For example, \(D_{i,1}D_{j,0}=1\) at the singleton assignment treating \(i\), whose probability is \(108/729\); subtracting \((4/27)(10/27)=40/729\) gives \(68/729\).  These entries prove the stated \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\), as well as exposure positivity and mutual exclusivity.

For Bernoulli \((1/2)\) marginals, \(\mu_a=1/2\) and \(\sigma_a^2=1/4\).  The countermonotone and comonotone quantile products give
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad
c_U=\frac14.
\]
Substitution in def:moment-matrix gives the displayed endpoint matrices.

For a normalized \(B(x,y)\), put
\[
s=\mathbf1^{\top}x,
\qquad
t=\mathbf1^{\top}y,
\qquad
q=x^{\top}y.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(0\le s^2,t^2\le9\).  Block multiplication gives
\[
S_B=
\begin{bmatrix}
\dfrac49-\dfrac{16s^2}{729}&-\dfrac{4q}{27}+\dfrac{68st}{729}\\
-\dfrac{4q}{27}+\dfrac{68st}{729}&\dfrac23+\dfrac{8t^2}{729}
\end{bmatrix},
\]
and, with
\[
d=729+12t^2-36s^2-54q^2+68qst-22s^2t^2,
\]
one has \(\det(S_B)=8d/19683\).  Membership in \(\mathcal B_{1/8}\) implies \(d>0\).  Direct multiplication in def:gain-loss yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
g_B(c_L)
&=\frac{76545+9891s^2+30732t^2-5832q^2+18232qst-10460s^2t^2}{1200d},\\
g_B(c_U)
&=\frac{3(66825-5181s^2-2652t^2-6048q^2+5968qst-1260s^2t^2)}{400d},
\end{aligned}                                                       \tag{1}
\]
and
\[
h(c_L)=\frac{313}{600},
\qquad
h(c_U)=\frac{171}{200}.                                              \tag{2}
\]

Since zero is the endpoint midpoint, \(g_B(0)=\{g_B(c_L)+g_B(c_U)\}/2\), and
\[
\frac{31}{80}-g_B(0)=\frac{N_0}{1200d},
\]
where
\[
N_0
=5022\left(q-\frac{1088}{2511}st\right)^2
+1629s^2+2148t^2-\frac{685118}{2511}s^2t^2.
\]
The last three terms are bilinear in \((s^2,t^2)\in[0,9]^2\); their four vertex values are
\[
0,
\qquad
14661,
\qquad
19332,
\qquad
\frac{368665}{31}.
\]
Bilinear interpolation and the square prove nonnegativity.  The bilinear term is strictly positive away from \((s^2,t^2)=(0,0)\), so equality holds exactly when \(s=t=q=0\).  Such pairs exist, and then \(S_B=\operatorname{diag}(4/9,2/3)\), so \(\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=4/27>1/8\).  This proves the full set \(\mathcal A_0\), and (1)--(2) give \(w(B_0)=521/1200\).

For minimax loss set \(\lambda=1407/2635\) and \(v=2613/8432\).  Since a maximum dominates a convex combination,
\[
w(B)-v
\ge\lambda\ell_B(c_L)+(1-\lambda)\ell_B(c_U)-v
=\frac{3N_{\mathrm{mm}}}{210800d},
\]
where
\[
N_{\mathrm{mm}}
=274734\left(q-\frac{70411}{137367}st\right)^2
+s^2\left(34527-\frac{439017980}{137367}t^2\right).
\]
Because \(t^2\le9\), the final coefficient is at least \(87967621/15263>0\).  Hence \(w(B)\ge v\).  Equality forces \(s=q=0\) and equality of the two endpoint losses.  At \(s=q=0\),
\[
\ell_B(c_L)-\ell_B(c_U)
=-\frac{3(55t^2-216)}{10(4t^2+243)},
\]
so equality holds exactly when \(t^2=216/55\).  These bases exist: choose a normalized \(y\) with that squared coordinate sum and then a normalized \(x\) orthogonal to \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1,y\}\).  Their \(S_B\) is diagonal with first entry \(4/9\), so their normalized smallest eigenvalue again equals \(4/27\).  This proves the asserted \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and value.

Finally, exposure positivity and the exhibited feasible bases put \(\xi_0\) in \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\).  The equality sets show
\[
\Delta(\xi_0)
=\frac{521}{1200}-\frac{2613}{8432}
=\frac{4912}{39525},
\qquad
\frac4{27}-\frac18=\frac5{216},
\]
uniformly over both optimizer correspondences. \(\square\)

statements.statement: Let \(E_1,E_0\) be compact metric spaces.  Under weak convergence of an ordered pair of marginal probability measures, the fixed-marginal coupling correspondence is continuous in the weak topology.  Consequently, for every continuous function \(\varphi:E_1\times E_0\to\mathbb R\), the minimum and maximum of \(H\mapsto\int\varphi\,dH\) over the coupling set vary continuously with the ordered marginal pair, and the associated optimizer correspondences are upper hemicontinuous.

source.locator: Main continuity theorem and the Berge maximum-theorem consequence, pp. 471--481
source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 1. Let X and Y be separable metrizable spaces and let φ : P(X) × P(Y) ⇉ P(X × Y) be defined: φ(μ,ν) = {τ ∈ P(X × Y) | τ_X = μ, τ_Y = ν}. The correspondence φ is continuous. According to Berge's maximum theorem, if W and Z are topological spaces and Φ : W ⇉ Z is a continuous correspondence with nonempty compact values, and f : W × Z → ℝ is continuous then (i) the function m(w) = max_{z∈Φ(w)} f(w,z) is continuous, and (ii) the correspondence β defined by β(w) = {z ∈ Z | f(w,z) = m(w)} is upper-hemicontinuous.

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity holds and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\) and both regular classes are nonempty, then
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}}w(B)
\le
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}}w(B).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
=
\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=
\inf_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B)).
\]
If the middle infimum is attained by some \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_Z\), then there is \(\kappa_0>0\) such that, for every \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\),
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
Thus the fixed-threshold values exhaust the entire maximal well-defined ordinary-inverse matrix domain in value through the quotient; singular or Moore--Penrose bases remain outside this conclusion.
statements.justification: This is the exact value transfer from fixed thresholds to the quotient and then to every ordinary-invertible matrix representative.
statements.gap: Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates does not introduce the normalized threshold family or prove value exhaustion and rescaling-fiber invariance.
statements.consumer: A solver can interpret its fixed-threshold optimum as an approximation to the best value over the full well-defined ordinary-inverse matrix domain.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
If \(0<\kappa_1\le\kappa_2\), then \(\mathcal B_{\kappa_2}\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa_1}\), so minimizing the same continuous loss over the larger compact set proves the first inequality.  Prop:kappa-exhaustion gives \(\mathcal B_Z=\bigcup_{\kappa>0}\mathcal B_\kappa\).  The infimum of a function over a union is the infimum of the infima over its nonempty members, whence
\[
\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B). \tag{1}
\]
Thm:zhao-ordinary-domain-quotient-transfer makes \(q_Z\) surjective and shows that \(w(q_Z(B))\) is constant on every fiber.  Hence
\[
\inf_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B))
=\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B), \tag{2}
\]
which proves the full value equality.

If \(B_Z^\star\) attains the quotient infimum, prop:kappa-exhaustion supplies \(\kappa_0>0\) with \(B_Z^\star\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_0}\).  For \(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0\),
\[
\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
\le\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)
\le w(B_Z^\star)
=\inf_{[B]\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
This proves equality.  Equations (1)--(2) concern only ordinary-invertible matrices and their rescaling quotient. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Define \(\iota:\mathcal B_Z\to\mathcal B_Z^+\) by \(\iota([B])=[B]_+\).  This map is a well-defined bijection from \(\mathcal B_Z\) onto
\[
 \{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:\operatorname{rank}(B^{\top}\Omega B)=2\}.
\]
For every \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\) and every \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\),
\[
 g_{\iota(B)}^+(c)=g_B(c),
 \qquad \ell_{\iota(B)}^+(c)=\ell_B(c),
 \qquad w^+(\iota(B))=w(B).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
If \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\), then \(S_B\succ0\), so both columns are nonzero and \(\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=2\).  Independent nonzero rescaling is the equivalence relation used both by the ordinary projective class and by the rank-two stratum of def:novel-pseudoinverse-completion.  Hence \([B]\mapsto[B]_+\) is well defined and injective.

Conversely, let \([C]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) have \(\operatorname{rank}(C^{\top}\Omega C)=2\).  The matrix \(C^{\top}\Omega C\) is a two-by-two positive-semidefinite matrix of full rank, hence positive definite.  Def:zhao-basis-class therefore gives \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\), and \(\iota([C])=[C]_+\).  This proves surjectivity onto the stated stratum.

On rank two, the Moore--Penrose inverse equals the ordinary inverse.  Substitution into def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss and def:gain-loss gives equality of gains for every feasible \(c\).  Subtracting from the common uncontrolled variance gives equality of endpoint losses, and taking their maximum gives \(w^+(\iota(B))=w(B)\). \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For \(e\in\{L,U\}\), set \(A_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\) and \(Z_B=\Omega^{1/2}B\).  Every \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) satisfies
\[
 g_B^+(c_e)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e),
 \qquad P_B=Z_B(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top},
\]
where \(P_B\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\), \(A_e\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(P_B)=\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\).  On rank two, \([B]_+=\iota([C])\) for a unique \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\), and the gains and losses agree.  If \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\), then for every singular \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) there is a sequence \([B_j]\in\mathcal B_Z\) such that
\[
 \limsup_{j\to\infty}w(B_j)\le w^+(B).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(e\in\{L,U\}\).  Def:moment-matrix gives \(Q(c_e)\succeq0\), and ass:exposure-positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) well defined.  Congruence gives
\[
A_e=\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1}Q(c_e)\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}\succeq0. \tag{1}
\]
Since \(S_B=Z_B^{\top}Z_B\), cyclicity of trace gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
n^2g_B^+(c_e)
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top}A_eZ_B\right]\\
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[Z_B(Z_B^{\top}Z_B)^+Z_B^{\top}A_e\right]
=\operatorname{tr}(P_BA_e).
\end{aligned} \tag{2}
\]
The singular-value decomposition of \(Z_B\) shows that \(P_B\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\) and has rank \(\operatorname{rank}(Z_B)=\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\).  The rank-two assertion follows from lem:zhao-rank-two-stratum-identification.

For the approximation, choose an actual block-separable representative \(B^\circ\) of the singular completion class and an actual representative \(C^\circ\) of any \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\).  Define
\[
B_t^\circ=B^\circ+tC^\circ.
\]
It remains block separable, and
\[
p(t)=\det\!\left\{(Z_{B^\circ}+tZ_{C^\circ})^{\top}(Z_{B^\circ}+tZ_{C^\circ})\right\}
\]
is a polynomial whose leading coefficient is \(\det(Z_{C^\circ}^{\top}Z_{C^\circ})>0\).  It therefore has only finitely many roots.  Choose \(t_j\downarrow0\) away from them, independently normalize the two nonzero columns of \(B_{t_j}^\circ\), and then pass to the ordinary quotient.  This gives \([B_j]\in\mathcal B_Z\); column normalization does not change its projector.

Along a subsequence, the rank-two projectors converge to an orthogonal projector \(P_\infty\).  If \(x=Z_{B^\circ}u\), then \((Z_{B^\circ}+t_jZ_{C^\circ})u\to x\) and belongs to \(\operatorname{range}(P_{B_j})\).  Hence
\[
\lVert P_{B_j}x-x\rVert
\le2\lVert x-(Z_{B^\circ}+t_jZ_{C^\circ})u\rVert\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{range}(P_B)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(P_\infty)\), so \(P_\infty-P_B\succeq0\).  From (1)--(2), simultaneously for both endpoints,
\[
\lim_jg_{B_j}(c_e)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(P_\infty A_e)
\ge g_B^+(c_e).
\]
The uncontrolled term is basis independent, so \(\limsup_j\ell_{B_j}(c_e)\le\ell_B^+(c_e)\).  Taking the maximum of the two endpoint losses proves \(\limsup_jw(B_j)\le w^+(B)\). \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:frechet-covariance-domain hold and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  For the novel Moore--Penrose completion of def:novel-pseudoinverse-completion,
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B).
\]
Writing \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\) for the fixed-threshold argmin, the rank-two completion minimizers are exactly
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\cap\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
=\iota\!\left(
\bigcup_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+}}
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\right).
\]
Possible singular ties are retained as the separate stratum
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\setminus\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1,\ w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\}.
\]
No existence of a singular tie is asserted, and no part of this completion is attributed to Zhao.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
For every \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\), lem:zhao-rank-two-stratum-identification gives \(w^+(\iota(C))=w(C)\).  Since \(\iota(C)\) is feasible in the novel completion,
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\le\inf_{C\in\mathcal B_Z}w(C). \tag{1}
\]
Conversely, a rank-two completion class is uniquely \(\iota(C)\), whereas every singular completion class admits, by lem:rank-stratified-projector-reduction, ordinary classes \(C_j\) with \(\limsup_jw(C_j)\le w^+(B)\).  Hence \(\inf_{C\in\mathcal B_Z}w(C)\le w^+(B)\) for every completion class.  Taking the minimum over that class and combining with (1) proves
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{C\in\mathcal B_Z}w(C).
\]
Prop:kappa-value-exhaustion gives the second equality.

If a rank-two completion minimizer equals \(\iota(C)\), prop:kappa-exhaustion supplies \(\kappa_C>0\) with \(C\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_C}\).  Then
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
\le\min_{A\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_C}}w(A)
\le w(C)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+,
\]
so \(C\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa_C)\) at a value-attaining threshold.  Conversely, every member of a fixed-threshold argmin whose value is \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) maps under \(\iota\) to a rank-two completion minimizer.  This proves the exact rank-two identity.  The final displayed set merely partitions the remaining equality set by rank; it retains possible singular ties and asserts no existence. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For the triangle matrices
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
and the endpoint matrices
\[
Q(c_L)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad A=\frac{I_3+J_3}{4},
\]
the rank-zero and rank-one strata of the novel Moore--Penrose completion obey the exact bounds
\[
\sup_{[B]_+\,:\,\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}g_B^+(0)
=\frac{87}{400}<\frac{31}{80}
\]
and
\[
\inf_{[B]_+\,:\,\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}w^+(B)
=\frac{39}{80}>\frac{2613}{8432}.
\]
More precisely, rank zero has \(g_B^+(0)=0\) and \(w^+(B)=171/200\).  In rank one, after normalizing the unique nonzero arm vector to squared norm three and writing \(u\) for the squared sum of its coordinates, so \(0\le u\le9\), the focal-only stratum has
\[
g_x^+(c_L)=\frac{1195u+6561}{1200(81-4u)},
\qquad g_x^+(c_U)=\frac{243(49-5u)}{400(81-4u)},
\]
whereas the comparison-only stratum has
\[
g_y^+(c_L)=\frac{1240u+729}{150(4u+243)},
\qquad g_y^+(c_U)=\frac{81(48-5u)}{50(4u+243)}.
\]
These rational formulas, together with \(0\le u\le9\), are an exact semialgebraic certificate for both displayed strict inequalities.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Write \(\mathbf1=\mathbf1_3\).  Simultaneous permutation decomposition into \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\) and \(\mathbf1^\perp\) reduces \(729\Omega\) to
\[
M_\parallel=\begin{bmatrix}60&96\\96&186\end{bmatrix},
\qquad M_\perp=\begin{bmatrix}108&-108\\-108&162\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Their leading entries are positive and their determinants are \(1944\) and \(5832\), so \(\Omega\succ0\).  Therefore rank zero means that both arm columns vanish, whereas rank one means that exactly one arm column is nonzero.

On the focal-only stratum normalize \(\lVert x\rVert_2^2=3\) and set \(u=(\mathbf1^{\top}x)^2\in[0,9]\).  The scalar Rayleigh quotient from lem:rank-stratified-projector-reduction gives
\[
g_x^+(c_L)=\frac{1195u+6561}{1200(81-4u)},
\qquad g_x^+(c_U)=\frac{243(49-5u)}{400(81-4u)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
g_x^+(0)=\frac{21141-1225u}{1200(81-4u)},
\qquad \frac{d}{du}g_x^+(0)=-\frac{4887}{400(4u-81)^2}<0.
\]
Using \(h(c_L)=313/600\) and \(h(c_U)=171/200\), the upper endpoint is always the worse loss and
\[
\ell_{x,U}=\frac{9(1755-17u)}{400(81-4u)},
\qquad \frac{d}{du}\ell_{x,U}=\frac{50787}{400(4u-81)^2}>0.
\]
Thus the focal-only maximum zero gain is \(87/400\), and its minimum worst loss is \(39/80\), both at \(u=0\).

On the comparison-only stratum, normalize \(\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3\) and use \(u=(\mathbf1^{\top}y)^2\in[0,9]\).  Direct substitution gives
\[
g_y^+(c_L)=\frac{1240u+729}{150(4u+243)},
\qquad g_y^+(c_U)=\frac{81(48-5u)}{50(4u+243)},
\]
and hence
\[
g_y^+(0)=\frac{25u+12393}{300(4u+243)},
\qquad \frac{d}{du}g_y^+(0)=-\frac{14499}{100(4u+243)^2}<0,
\]
while the upper endpoint is again worse and
\[
\ell_{y,U}=\frac{9(256u+2889)}{200(4u+243)},
\qquad \frac{d}{du}\ell_{y,U}=\frac{113967}{50(4u+243)^2}>0.
\]
Thus the comparison-only extrema are \(17/100\) and \(107/200\).  Rank zero has zero gain and worst loss \(171/200\).  Comparing all three singular cases yields
\[
\sup_{\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}g_B^+(0)=\frac{87}{400}<\frac{31}{80},
\qquad
\inf_{\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}w^+(B)=\frac{39}{80}>\frac{2613}{8432}.
\]
Every denominator is positive on \([0,9]\), so all boundary cases are included. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) be the maximal block-separable matrix domain on which the ordinary inverse in Zhao's Equation (8) is defined, and let \(q_Z(B)=[B]\).  Then \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) is surjective, and
\[
q_Z(B)=q_Z(C)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
C=B\operatorname{diag}(t_1,t_0)
\quad\text{for some }t_1t_0\ne0.
\]
For every such diagonal \(T\), every \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), and every \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\),
\[
g_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=g_{q_Z(B)}(c),\qquad
\ell_{q_Z(BT)}(c)=\ell_{q_Z(B)}(c),\qquad
w(q_Z(BT))=w(q_Z(B)).
\]
Consequently, for every nonempty \(K\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\), the infima and suprema of each displayed pullback criterion over \(q_Z^{-1}(K)\) equal those over \(K\), and every attained argmin or argmax correspondence on the matrix domain is exactly the inverse image under \(q_Z\) of its quotient correspondence.  This is an exact quotient transfer for the ordinary-inverse domain implicit in Zhao's formula; it neither defines nor attributes a singular Moore--Penrose domain to Zhao.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
If \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\), then \(S_B\succ0\), so each arm column is nonzero and def:zhao-basis-class defines \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\).  Conversely, every \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\) has a block-separable representative with \(C^{\top}\Omega C\succ0\), hence a preimage in \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\).  Thus \(q_Z\) is onto.  The definition of the projective quotient says exactly that two representatives have the same class if and only if \(C=BT\) for a diagonal \(T=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,t_0)\) with \(t_1t_0\ne0\), proving the fiber formula.

For such \(T\),
\[
S_{BT}=T^{\top}S_BT,
\qquad
S_{BT}^{-1}=T^{-1}S_B^{-1}(T^{\top})^{-1}. \tag{1}
\]
Substitute (1) and \(BT\) into def:gain-loss.  Cyclicity of trace cancels \(T\) and \(T^{-1}\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
n^2g_{q_Z(BT)}(c)
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[T^{-1}S_B^{-1}(T^{\top})^{-1}
T^{\top}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega BT\right]\\
&=\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right]
=n^2g_{q_Z(B)}(c).
\end{aligned}
\]
The uncontrolled term \(h(c)\) does not depend on \(B\), so the endpoint losses and their maximum are invariant as well.  An invariant function is constant on every fiber of a surjection.  Its image values over \(q_Z^{-1}(K)\) therefore equal its values over \(K\), proving equality of infima and suprema; if an extremum is attained, a matrix is an optimizer exactly when its quotient class is, giving the inverse-image correspondence. \(\square\)

Let \(\xi_0\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\) and suppose that, for some \(\eta>0\),
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}\ge\eta.
\]
For every sequence \((\xi_j)_{j\ge1}\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) converging to \(\xi_0\) in the relative topology of def:lawful-instance-class,
\[
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)\ge\Delta(\xi_0).
\]
statements.justification: This quantitative lower-semicontinuity lemma is the reusable step that turns an exact optimizer-wide slack certificate into a uniform dominance margin.
statements.gap: Bergin1999RestrictedMarginals supplies continuity of the fixed-marginal coupling correspondence; the new step propagates that continuity through the moving regular projective feasible set and both optimizer correspondences.
statements.consumer: The triangle neighborhood corollary uses the lemma to preserve half of the exact rational separation margin.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Let \(\xi_j=(\nu_j,F_{1j},F_{0j})\to\xi_0\).  Use normalized representatives in the fixed compact product of the two radius-\(\sqrt n\) spheres modulo independent sign changes; this is the compact representation supplied by prop:kappa-exhaustion.  Because the assignment space is finite, total-variation convergence of \(\nu_j\) implies entrywise convergence
\[
\Pi_j\longrightarrow\Pi_0,
\qquad
\Omega_j\longrightarrow\Omega_0.                                    \tag{1}
\]
Exposure positivity at \(\xi_0\) implies that every relevant diagonal entry of \(\Pi_j\) is uniformly bounded away from zero for all sufficiently large \(j\), and hence
\[
\Pi_j^{-1}\longrightarrow\Pi_0^{-1}.                                \tag{2}
\]

Wasserstein convergence on \([0,1]\) implies weak convergence and convergence of first and second moments.  Apply lem:restricted-marginal-extrema-continuity with \(\varphi(y_1,y_0)=y_1y_0\).  The minimum and maximum cross moments over the coupling sets converge.  Subtracting the convergent products of marginal means yields
\[
c_{Lj}\longrightarrow c_{L0},
\qquad
c_{Uj}\longrightarrow c_{U0}.                                       \tag{3}
\]
Def:moment-matrix and convergence of the marginal first and second moments then give
\[
Q_j(c_{ej})\longrightarrow Q_0(c_{e0})
\qquad(e\in\{L,U\}).                                                \tag{4}
\]

For a normalized basis \(B\), put
\[
\rho(\xi,B)=\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega(\xi)B\}.
\]
This function is jointly continuous by (1).  On the closed region \(\rho\ge\kappa\), the inverse exists and satisfies
\[
\lVert S_B^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le(n\kappa)^{-1}.               \tag{5}
\]
Equations (1)--(5), def:gain-loss, and the endpoint reduction of thm:fixed-basis-endpoints show that \(g_{B,\xi}(0)\), both endpoint losses, and \(w_\xi(B)\) are jointly continuous on this region.

Choose \(B^\star_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\), which exists because ass:kappa-feasibility and prop:kappa-exhaustion make the feasible set nonempty and compact.  The assumed slack gives
\(\rho(\xi_0,B^\star_{\mathrm{mm}})\ge\kappa+\eta\), so this fixed representative is feasible for all sufficiently large \(j\).  Therefore
\[
\limsup_{j\to\infty}v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_j)
\le\lim_{j\to\infty}w_{\xi_j}(B^\star_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0).                                           \tag{6}
\]

For each \(j\), compactness and continuity allow a choice
\[
B_{0j}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B).
\]
Choose a subsequence that realizes the lower limit of these minimum values and, by compactness, a further subsequence such that \(B_{0j}\to\bar B_0\).  Closedness of the inequality \(\rho\ge\kappa\) makes \(\bar B_0\) feasible at \(\xi_0\).  Choose any \(C_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)\).  Its assumed slack makes it feasible for all sufficiently large \(j\), and the defining optimality of \(B_{0j}\) for the zero-covariance criterion gives
\[
g_{B_{0j},\xi_j}(0)\ge g_{C_0,\xi_j}(0).
\]
Passing to the limit shows \(g_{\bar B_0,\xi_0}(0)\ge g_{C_0,\xi_0}(0)\).  Since \(C_0\) already attains the feasible maximum and \(\bar B_0\) is feasible, equality holds and \(\bar B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)\).  Joint continuity now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_j)}w_{\xi_j}(B)
&=w_{\xi_0}(\bar B_0)\\
&\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B).
\end{aligned}                                                       \tag{7}
\]
The subsequence was selected to realize the lower limit, so (7) holds for the original sequence.

Finally, def:dominance-gap, (6), (7), and the elementary inequality \(\liminf(a_j-b_j)\ge\liminf a_j-\limsup b_j\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)
&\ge
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\\
&=\Delta(\xi_0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Every division, inverse, moving-feasible-set comparison, and boundary passage is justified respectively by exposure positivity, the \(\kappa\)-bound, compactness, and the stated optimizer-wide slack. \(\square\)
