For the explicit triangle instance \(\xi_0\) and \(\kappa=1/8\) in thm:triangle-minimax-separation-certificate, there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) containing \(\xi_0\) such that
\[
\Delta(\xi)>\frac{\delta}{2}=\frac{2456}{39525}
\qquad(\xi\in\mathcal U),
\]
where \(\delta=4912/39525\).  Consequently, for every \(\xi\in\mathcal U\), every \(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\), and every \(B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)\),
\[
w_\xi(B_{\mathrm{mm}})<w_\xi(B_0).
\]
statements.justification: The explicit witness becomes a nondegenerate region of lawful designs and marginals, with a retained rational performance margin.
statements.gap: Neither Zhao2026OptimalControlVariates nor general dependence-robust optimization results give a strict full-correspondence comparison between the minimax and zero-covariance basis rules on an open family of network experiments.
statements.consumer: Nearby lawful network experiments inherit the guarantee that every minimax optimizer has lower worst-copula residual variance than every zero-covariance optimizer.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Thm:triangle-minimax-separation-certificate gives
\[
\Delta(\xi_0)=\delta=\frac{4912}{39525}>0
\]
and optimizer-wide slack \(\eta=5/216>0\).  Thm:relative-open-persistence first yields a relative-open neighborhood with positive gap.  To retain half the exact margin, suppose for contradiction that every relative-open neighborhood of \(\xi_0\) contained an instance with gap at most \(\delta/2\).  Metrizability then supplies a sequence \(\xi_j\to\xi_0\) with \(\Delta(\xi_j)\le\delta/2\).  Lem:dominance-gap-lower-semicontinuity would give
\[
\delta=\Delta(\xi_0)
\le\liminf_{j\to\infty}\Delta(\xi_j)
\le\frac\delta2,
\]
which is impossible.  Hence some relative-open \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) satisfies \(\Delta(\xi)>\delta/2=2456/39525\).

For any indicated optimizers, def:dominance-gap and the fact that every minimax optimizer has loss \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
w_\xi(B_0)-w_\xi(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
&\ge
\inf_{C_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi)}w_\xi(C_0)
-\sup_{C\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)}w_\xi(C)\\
&=\Delta(\xi)>\frac\delta2>0.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the strict full-correspondence comparison. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness whose strict separation survives every singular stratum of the novel Moore--Penrose completion.  Let \(n=3\), let
\[
G=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&1\\1&1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\nu(w)=\left(\frac13\right)^{\sum_iw_i}
       \left(\frac23\right)^{3-\sum_iw_i},
\]
and, writing \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact inputs are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For normalized rank-two representatives \(B(x,y)\),
\[
\mathcal A_0=\{[B(x,y)]:\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,
\ \mathbf1^{\top}x=\mathbf1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\{[B(x,y)]:\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,
\ \mathbf1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,
\ (\mathbf1^{\top}y)^2=216/55\}.
\]
They are nonempty, lie in \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), and satisfy
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\quad w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200},
\quad w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432},
\quad \lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}
\]
on the respective equality sets.  Under the rank-two bijection \(\iota:\mathcal B_Z\to\mathcal B_Z^+\), the optimizer sets and values on the full novel completion, including ranks zero and one, are exactly
\[
\mathcal A_0^+=\iota(\mathcal A_0),
\qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\iota(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}),
\]
\[
\max_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\min_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)=\frac{2613}{8432};
\]
in particular, there are no singular optimizer ties.  Consequently \(\xi_0=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\in\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and
\[
\delta=\frac{4912}{39525},\qquad \eta=\frac5{216}
\]
give the ordinary and completion full-correspondence gaps and the optimizer-wide regularity slack asserted by def:dominance-gap.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The exact assignment enumeration, endpoint calculation, and rank-two optimization in thm:triangle-minimax-separation-certificate give the displayed \(\Pi\), \(\Omega\), \(c_L,c_U\), endpoint moment matrices, the full ordinary equality sets, and the values
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad
w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200},
\qquad
v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432}.                                  \tag{1}
\]
Those polynomial certificates use the \(\kappa\)-restriction only to license inversion.  The displayed \(\Omega\) is positive definite by lem:triangle-completion-singular-strata-certificate, so every normalized rank-two block basis has \(S_B\succ0\).  The same equality calculations therefore apply over the entire rank-two stratum of def:novel-pseudoinverse-completion.  Lem:zhao-rank-two-stratum-identification transfers the equality sets through \(\iota\) without changing gains or losses.

It remains to exclude singular ties.  Lem:triangle-completion-singular-strata-certificate proves
\[
\sup_{\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}g_B^+(0)
=\frac{87}{400}<\frac{31}{80}                                       \tag{2}
\]
and
\[
\inf_{\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1}w^+(B)
=\frac{39}{80}>\frac{2613}{8432}.                                   \tag{3}
\]
Thus no rank-zero or rank-one completion class is a zero-covariance or minimax optimizer.  Combining (1)--(3) with rank-two identification gives
\[
\mathcal A_0^+=\iota(\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\iota(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}),
\]
and the stated completion values; in particular, there is no singular optimizer tie.

Every ordinary optimizer in either equality set satisfies \(\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=4/27\), while \(\kappa=1/8\).  Exposure positivity and the explicit feasible bases therefore put \(\xi_0\) in \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and the full-correspondence certificates are
\[
\delta
=\frac{521}{1200}-\frac{2613}{8432}
=\frac{4912}{39525}>0,
\qquad
\eta=\frac4{27}-\frac18=\frac5{216}>0.
\]
The loss identity under \(\iota\) makes the same separation valid on the rank-two optimizer sets in the note's novel completion. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For the explicit triangle instance \(\xi_0\) and \(\kappa=1/8\) in thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate, there is a relative-open neighborhood \(\mathcal U\subset\mathfrak X_\kappa\) containing \(\xi_0\) such that
\[
\Delta(\xi)>\frac{\delta}{2}=\frac{2456}{39525}
\qquad(\xi\in\mathcal U).
\]
Throughout \(\mathcal U\), the completion optimizer correspondences contain no singular classes and satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_0^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi(\mathcal A_0(\xi)),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)).
\]
Consequently every ordinary minimax optimizer has lower worst-copula loss than every ordinary zero-covariance optimizer, and every completion minimax optimizer has lower worst-copula loss than every completion zero-covariance optimizer, with each difference exceeding \(\delta/2\).
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
At \(\xi_0\), thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate gives the ordinary gap \(\delta>0\), optimizer-wide slack \(\eta>0\), and the strict singular-stratum gaps
\[
\frac{31}{80}-\frac{87}{400}=\frac{17}{100}>0,
\qquad
\frac{39}{80}-\frac{2613}{8432}=\frac{468}{2635}>0.                 \tag{1}
\]
We first show that the rank statements in (1) persist.  Total-variation convergence of the assignment law on its finite support makes \(\Pi\) and \(\Omega\) continuous.  Exposure positivity makes \(\Pi^{-1}\) continuous on a neighborhood of \(\xi_0\).  Wasserstein convergence of the bounded marginals gives convergence of their first and second moments, while lem:restricted-marginal-extrema-continuity gives convergence of the two covariance endpoints.  Def:moment-matrix then gives convergence of both endpoint moment matrices.  The triangle matrix \(\Omega(\xi_0)\) is positive definite, so, after restricting to a relative-open neighborhood, \(\Omega(\xi)\) remains uniformly positive definite.

Under the normalization in def:novel-pseudoinverse-completion, the rank-zero component is a singleton, each rank-one component is a radius-\(\sqrt n\) sphere modulo sign, and the rank-two component is a product of two such quotients.  These are compact components distinguished by which arm columns vanish.  When \(\Omega(\xi)\succ0\), the rank of \(S_B\) is constant on each component.  On rank zero the criteria are explicit constants; on rank one the Moore--Penrose formula is a scalar inverse with denominator bounded away from zero by uniform positive definiteness; and on rank two it is an ordinary inverse whose smallest eigenvalue is uniformly positive on the compact normalized component.  Hence def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss makes \(g_B^+(0)\) and \(w^+(B)\) jointly continuous on every component, uniformly on compact neighborhoods.  Taking maxima or minima over a fixed compact component preserves continuity of the componentwise optimum value.  The two strict inequalities in (1) therefore persist on a smaller relative-open neighborhood.  Every completion optimizer of either criterion consequently has rank two there.

Next we show that every such optimizer lies strictly inside the \(\kappa\)-regular ordinary class.  If this failed arbitrarily near \(\xi_0\), there would be \(\xi_j\to\xi_0\) and rank-two completion optimizers \(B_j\) for one of the two criteria such that
\[
\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}S_{B_j}(\xi_j)\}<\kappa+\frac\eta2.
\]
Compactness of the normalized rank-two component supplies a convergent subsequence \(B_j\to\bar B\).  Joint continuity, together with comparison to every fixed completion basis, shows that \(\bar B\) is an optimizer of the same criterion at \(\xi_0\).  Thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate identifies every such optimizer with an ordinary optimizer and gives normalized eigenvalue at least \(\kappa+\eta\), contradicting the preceding display after passage to the limit.  Thus every nearby completion optimizer has normalized eigenvalue at least \(\kappa+\eta/2\) and has an ordinary preimage in \(\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi)\).

Lem:zhao-rank-two-stratum-identification preserves the two criteria under this preimage.  Because the global completion optimum is attained inside \(\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi)\), its value equals the corresponding optimum over \(\mathcal B_\kappa(\xi)\).  Both inclusions of optimizer sets follow, giving
\[
\mathcal A_0^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi\{\mathcal A_0(\xi)\},
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+(\xi)=\iota_\xi\{\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi)\}. \tag{2}
\]

Finally, the freshly established lem:dominance-gap-lower-semicontinuity and the exact gap at \(\xi_0\) imply, by the same sequential contradiction argument, that a still smaller relative-open neighborhood satisfies
\[
\Delta(\xi)>\frac\delta2=\frac{2456}{39525}.
\]
For every ordinary zero-covariance optimizer and every ordinary minimax optimizer, their loss difference is at least \(\Delta(\xi)\), hence exceeds \(\delta/2\).  Equation (2) and preservation of loss under \(\iota_\xi\) give the identical conclusion for every pair of completion optimizers. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
For the triangle instance of thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate, optimization over the full maximal well-defined unquotiented ordinary-inverse domain \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) has
\[
\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}g_{q_Z(B)}(0)=q_Z^{-1}(\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B))=q_Z^{-1}(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}),
\]
where \(\mathcal A_0\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are exactly the displayed normalized equality sets in that theorem.  Their values are respectively \(31/80\) and \(2613/8432\); every zero-covariance optimizer has worst-copula loss \(521/1200\), so the exact worst-loss reduction is
\[
\frac{521}{1200}-\frac{2613}{8432}=\frac{4912}{39525}>0.
\]
Thus the triangle separation holds on the entire ordinary-inverse matrix domain implicit in Zhao's Equation (8), with optimizer sets enlarged only by independent nonzero column rescaling.  The separate singular-stratum conclusions concern only the note's novel Moore--Penrose completion.
statements.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate proves that the complete rank-two quotient equality sets are \(\mathcal A_0\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\), with zero-covariance gain \(31/80\), zero-covariance-optimizer worst loss \(521/1200\), and minimax worst loss \(2613/8432\).  Every member of \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) maps to a rank-two quotient class.  Thm:zhao-ordinary-domain-quotient-transfer says that both gain and loss are constant on the independent nonzero column-rescaling fibers and that the matrix-domain optimizer correspondences are exactly the inverse images of their quotient correspondences.  Therefore
\[
\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}g_{q_Z(B)}(0)
=q_Z^{-1}(\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B))
=q_Z^{-1}(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}),
\]
and all three values are preserved.  Subtraction gives
\[
\frac{521}{1200}-\frac{2613}{8432}
=\frac{4912}{39525}>0.
\]
Thus the exact separation extends to the entire maximal ordinary-inverse matrix domain, with no change other than duplication along rescaling fibers.  No singular class is used in this transfer. \(\square\)

statements.statement:
Endpoint covariances alone do not determine the minimax worst-copula residual value.  In particular, let \(n=3\), let \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\) variables under \(\nu\), and set \(f_i(w)=w_i\).  With \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\varepsilon=1/100\), the marginal pairs \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\) and \((F_1,F_0)=(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\delta_0)\) produce the same moment-incomplete tuple
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,\qquad
\Omega=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix},
\qquad c_L=c_U=0,
\]
but their endpoint moment matrices differ and their minimax residual values are, respectively,
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\frac1{36}.
\]
Consequently, no algorithm whose only input is \((\Pi,\Omega,c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon)\) can always return rational bounds
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon.
\]
Thus endpoint moment matrices such as \(Q(c_L)\) and \(Q(c_U)\), or equivalent marginal moments, are necessary inputs for the proposed certification problem.  This obstruction makes no claim that the corrected moment-complete branch-and-bound solver terminates at every positive tolerance.

Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility hold.  The primary minimax correspondence is nonempty and satisfies the unconditional weak worst-copula dominance certificate
\[
\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}}w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm}}
\le
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0}w(B_0).
\]
Strict inequality is not universal and requires a separate lawful witness.

Let \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\).  Under ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, ass:frechet-covariance-domain, and ass:product-coupling-zero,
\[
h(c)=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
w(B)=h(0)+\max\left\{\frac{2c_L}{n}-g_B(c_L),\frac{2c_U}{n}-g_B(c_U)\right\}.
\]
If \(c_L<c_U\), minimization of \(w(B)\) is not algebraically equivalent to maximization of \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\): as functions of a formal endpoint-gain pair \((x_L,x_U)\), the two loss criteria are not related by a constant independent of \((x_L,x_U)\).

For every moment-complete input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying exposure positivity and \(\kappa\)-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the candidate projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad
U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
Here \(B_{\varepsilon}\in\mathcal B_\kappa\) is represented exactly, including when the feasible set has no relative interior and lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  A chart box meeting that equality boundary is never discarded as infeasible; it may be discarded only when its certified objective lower bound exceeds the incumbent upper bound.  Consequently, along any sequence \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and retained-box mesh diameters converge to zero.  This is a finite, instance-dependent termination result; it asserts neither a uniform complexity bound nor a semidefinite-program reduction.

For every rational or real-algebraic input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the algebraic projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a locally checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
 L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
 \qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
The incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\) has finite real-algebraic coordinates, including when every feasible point lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  The checker verifies only CAD sign certificates, algebraic feasibility, outward objective bounds, rational norm and diameter records, chart cover, pruning inequalities, and mesh; the displayed facts about \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are mathematical consequences.  Along every \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and meshes converge to zero.  No uniform complexity bound or semidefinite-program reduction is asserted.

For every rational signed pivot-chart box, intersection with the normalized feasible set \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is an existential semialgebraic question.  More explicitly, sphere feasibility, chart and box restrictions, and \(S_B-n\kappa I_2\succeq0\) are finitely many polynomial equalities and weak inequalities with rational or real-algebraic coefficients; for
\[
 S_B-n\kappa I_2=\begin{bmatrix}u&v\\v&z\end{bmatrix},
\]
the matrix inequality is exactly \(u\ge0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(uz-v^2\ge0\).  Cylindrical algebraic decomposition therefore terminates with either an exact real-algebraic feasible sample or a finite infeasibility certificate, including when feasibility occurs only on the equality boundary.

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite network \(G\), known assignment law \(\nu\), known exposure maps \(f_i\), and two mutually exclusive exposure events.
sampling_model.units: The realized finite-population potential outcomes are fixed for design-based estimation; the i.i.d. law \(H\) is used only to choose the basis ex ante.
sampling_model.treatment: The main experiment draws \(W\sim\nu\), and assignment is the only randomness in the causal estimator conditional on the chosen basis.
sampling_model.overlap: Every exposure probability \(\pi_{i,a}\) is positive, and basis covariance is bounded below by \(\kappa\) on the optimization class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Two arm-specific external or historical i.i.d. samples are mutually unpaired and independent of the later assignment; they estimate \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), while the cross-world copula is neither estimated nor assumed.

tldr: Rare network exposures make Horvitz--Thompson estimation noisy, and Zhao's optimal indicator control variates reduce this design variance, but the ex ante basis depends on a cross-world covariance that an unpaired pilot cannot identify. The contribution chain imports the sharp Fréchet covariance range, proves a new fixed-basis affine worst-copula reduction inside Zhao's objective, poses certified global maximin optimization on the fixed-\(\kappa\) projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency without assuming away ties. Neighborhood persistence is supporting and witness-gated; no strict-dominance region is claimed unless the full-correspondence separation-and-slack certificate is produced.

project_justification.fill: The project imports the sharp endpoint formulas, proves their affine worst-copula and zero-surrogate frontier inside Zhao's fixed-basis objective, formulates a computably specified global maximin certificate on the compact \(\kappa\)-regular projective class, and proves uniform plug-in value and outer argmax-correspondence consistency. Conditional persistence is supporting: a strict-dominance region requires a separate certified witness with both separation and optimizer-wide \(\kappa\)-slack.
